plans.note: Section 9 is the express limitation of liability; check mutuality, cap size (likely tied to fees paid), consequential-damages waiver and carve-outs for indemnity (sec-8-2) and confidentiality (sec-10).

Section 8 (INDEMNIFICATION) should carry Commerce One's IP infringement indemnity in favour of Corio as licensee/host; confirm scope, defence/control, and that any Corio-side indemnity stays narrow, and check interaction with the liability cap in sec-9.

Look for restrictions on Corio hosting or reselling competing procurement applications in the grant of rights (sec-3, TERRITORY / CORIO MARKET SEGMENT definitions in sec-1-2), shared resources (sec-13) and the sales and marketing exhibit (sec-20).

Check whether the grant of rights or the marketing cooperation exhibit obliges Corio to source procurement software exclusively from Commerce One or to lead with its product; defined terms CORIO MARKET SEGMENT and TERRITORY are the likely hooks.

Pricing (Exhibit B, sec-p0148/sec-p0155) and Fees (sec-4) are the only plausible homes for a most-favoured-pricing term; flag only if it runs against us (i.e., Corio must give Commerce One best terms). Likely no MFN at all.
Non-solicits usually sit in Miscellaneous (sec-14) or alongside confidentiality (sec-10); if present, check mutuality, duration and a general-advertising carve-out. Probably absent.
Section 11 (TERM AND TERMINATION) — check for a convenience right for Corio, cure periods, and whether Commerce One can terminate mid-term or on breach without cure.
Initial term, auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window should be in sec-11; any renewal-period price uplift may appear in Exhibit B pricing (sec-p0148) or payment terms (sec-17).

Governing law, venue and any dispute resolution provision will be in MISCELLANEOUS (sec-14); the defined term RULES suggests an arbitration clause — verify forum and that California/New York/Delaware law applies.
Assignment/change-of-control language sits in sec-14; confirm Corio may assign to affiliates and successors and that Commerce One has no termination right on our change of control.

Ownership/reservation of rights should be in GRANT OF RIGHTS (sec-3); check the DEVELOPMENTS and EMPLOYEE NDA/INVENTION AGREEMENT definitions (sec-1-2) for assignment of Corio-created work or customer data to Commerce One; trademarks in sec-6 and escrow materials in sec-12.

Section 2 GRANT OF RIGHTS (sec-3) plus DELIVERY (sec-3-2) and the SOFTWARE/DEMONSTRATION SOFTWARE/CUSTOMERS definitions — confirm the hosting licence extends to Corio affiliates, contractors and Corio's Customers and is not revocable at will.
Any audit of Corio's usage or revenue-share reporting would sit in FEES (sec-4) or Exhibit B payment terms (sec-17); check frequency, notice, on-site scope and who bears cost.

Watch for late-payment penalties, early-termination charges or shortfall payments in sec-4/sec-17 and sec-11; service credits running to Corio are acceptable. Likely no true liquidated damages against us.

Section 7 WARRANTIES AND DISCLAIMER (sec-8) — check the Warranty Period length, the remedy, and the breadth of the disclaimer; supporting obligations in maintenance (sec-5), Acceptance Test (sec-3-2) and the Exhibit C support outline (sec-p0171).
No insurance heading in the outline; if anything exists it would be in MISCELLANEOUS (sec-14) or attached to the indemnity (sec-8-2). Expect to raise as missing.
Check FEES (sec-4) and Exhibit B pricing/revenue sharing (sec-p0148, sec-p0155, sec-17) for minimum licence fees, guaranteed revenue-share floors or committed user counts, and whether an exit exists.

Effect-of-termination provisions in sec-11 (wind-down for Corio's Customers, data return) and the SOURCE CODE ESCROW section (sec-12) are the likely sources; confirm a continuity/transition period rather than immediate cut-off.
